description:
STEP 1 (build beside the old). Wire the construction root to emit the canonical arrow.

Code-review finding (proposal "Where it is built"): resolve.rs already does the one traversal. resolve_pair threads vars: HashMap<String,TypeVarId> and ALREADY builds a structural shadow beside every Ty (a ResolvedTypeShape: Var(id)/Arrow{params,result}/Tuple, recursing into arrows) "so their variable numbering can never drift apart" -- and resolve_spec_decl DISCARDS it (resolve.rs:189). Numbering today is deterministic first-occurrence (TypeVarId(vars.len()), vars.entry(name).or_insert(next)), NOT arbitrary. So the construction root is half-built: it computes positional structure and throws it away.

Work: number the shadow by ADDRESS (not by encounter), keep it, and emit:
  resolve_spec_decl(spec) -> ResolvedArrow { arrow: Ty (interned canonical), names: Map<Address,Name> (ephemeral, diagnostics), bounds: Map<Address,Ty> (ephemeral, contract application) }

Code-review finding 5 (must be honored): TWO resolvers feed ResolvedSpecDecl -- compiler2/resolve.rs AND legacy type_expr/env.rs -- and 6+ consumers (extern + ir_lower included) destructure {params,result,constraints}. Unify on the kept shadow; account for BOTH resolvers and every consumer. Moderate-to-high blast radius, not localized.

Names and bounds resolve THROUGH the name->address map and stop at the semantics boundary; they never enter the interned type.

Depends on: addressed-arrow machinery (fz-hwn.27.2).
Checks: spec-resolution unit tests assert the emitted arrow + name/bound sidecars for the proposal examples; both resolver paths covered; lib green, zero warnings.

comments.text: Carries its own Trash mark: rename ResolvedSpecDecl{params,result,constraints} with the trash_ trigger as it is superseded by ResolvedArrow (deferred here from fz-hwn.27.1 -- trait/field coupling, see 27.1 comment).

title: resolve.rs emits ResolvedArrow{arrow,names,bounds}; keep+address the discarded shape shadow
